Response times and rapid guessing

Source: vignettes/response-times.Rmd
response-times.Rmd

Computer-based tests record how long each response took. mirtverse uses those times together with a fitted mirt model, following van der Linden’s (2007) hierarchical framework:

  • Time intensity (βj\beta_j): how long item j takes on average (log scale).
  • Time discrimination (αj\alpha_j): how consistently the item’s times reflect a person’s speed.
  • Speed (τi\tau_i): how fast person i works, correlated with ability θi\theta_i.
library(mirtverse)

Simulated example

sim_rt() generates responses and response times; here 8% of examinees rapid-guess on some items.

sim <- sim_rt(N = 1500, J = 20, rho = -0.3, rapid = 0.08, seed = 2026)
mod <- mirt(sim$responses, 1, verbose = FALSE)
fit <- fit_rt(mod, sim$rt)
fit

#>   (median 33.0 s). 
#> 
#> Rapid responding
#> ----------------
#> * 2.9% of responses were flagged as rapid (residual method); 8.0% of
#>   examinees have response time effort below .90. 
#> * Consider filtering low-effort examinees (motivation filtering) or
#>   down-weighting rapid responses before reporting scores. 
#> 
#> Person fit
#> ----------
#> * 8.0% of examinees have aberrant overall timing (l_t p < .05), against 5%
#>   expected by chance.

Rapid guessing

Several rules are available. The default "residual" rule flags a response that is much faster than expected for that person on that item. The normative threshold rules "nt10", "nt15" and "nt20" flag responses faster than 10%, 15% or 20% of the item’s mean time, with each threshold capped at 10 seconds (Wise & Ma, 2012). Change the cap with nt_max, or set nt_max = Inf to drop it. The item thresholds are stored in fit$thresholds.

mean(fit$flags[sim$rapid])   # share of simulated rapid guesses detected
#> [1] 1
mean(fit$flags[!sim$rapid])  # false alarms
#> [1] 0.004781421
autoplot(fit, "rapid")

autoplot(fit, "rte")

Response time effort (RTE) is each examinee’s share of non-rapid responses (Wise & Kong, 2005). Examinees below .90 are often excluded before reporting group results (motivation filtering).

persons <- augment(fit)
head(persons)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 9
#>    theta se_theta theta_responses_only     tau se_tau  n_rt   rte     lt

Notes

The item response parameters are taken from the mirt model and held fixed; the response-time parameters, speed variance and ability-speed correlation are estimated by marginal maximum likelihood. Because times act as collateral information, the joint ability estimates (theta) can be slightly more precise than the response-only estimates (theta_responses_only) when ability and speed are strongly correlated.

References

van der Linden, W. J. (2007). A hierarchical framework for modeling speed and accuracy on test items. Psychometrika, 72, 287-308.

Wise, S. L., & Kong, X. (2005). Response time effort: A new measure of examinee motivation in computer-based tests. Applied Measurement in Education, 18, 163-183.
